title: Megatron-LM: Training Multi-Billion Parameter Language Models Using Model Parallelism
authors: Mohammad Shoeybi, Mostofa Patwary, Raul Puri, Patrick LeGresley, Jared Casper, Bryan Catanzaro
run_label: watch a layer split across GPUs

code.title: NVIDIA/Megatron-LM
code.note: the authors' code (repo, about 25 minutes for the README and entry path); still developed, now as Megatron-Core, and the reference implementation of everything in the paper

takeaway: Introduced tensor (intra-layer model) parallelism: column-split the GEMM feeding each nonlinearity and row-split the one after it, so a transformer layer needs only 4 all-reduces, enabling an 8.3B GPT-2 on 512 V100s at 76% scaling efficiency.

headline.k: GPT-2-style model on 512 V100s, 8-way tensor × 64-way data parallel
2 forward and 2 backward, for attention and MLP together
headline.d: the whole of the communication the split adds

resources.n: the clearest modern walkthrough of column- and row-parallel linears, with communication-cost analysis and profiles.

resources.t: How to Train Really Large Models on Many GPUs?
resources.n: situates Megatron-style tensor parallelism among the other parallelism and memory-saving techniques.

resources.t: Efficient Large-Scale Language Model Training on GPU Clusters Using Megatron-LM
resources.n: the follow-up: this paper's tensor parallelism combined with pipeline and data parallelism (PTD-P) and an interleaved 1F1B schedule, 502 PFLOP/s on 3,072 A100s.

resources.t: Reducing Activation Recomputation in Large Transformer Models
resources.n: sequence parallelism: the same f and g idea, with each all-reduce split into a reduce-scatter and an all-gather so LayerNorm and dropout are no longer duplicated.

kb.n: 2017: the layer structure being partitioned (attention heads and a two-matrix MLP).
2018: the architecture whose LayerNorm and residual placement this paper changes to scale it past 336M.
2019, a month later: the memory-side alternative, sharding optimizer state, gradients and weights under data parallelism instead of splitting layers; Turing-NLG used both.
2020: trained with "a mixture of model parallelism within each matrix multiply and model parallelism across the layers", at the scale this line of work enabled.
2021: expert parallelism, the axis that later replaced tensor parallelism in some MoE training runs.
2024: 4D parallelism with tensor parallelism of 8 inside each NVLink machine, citing this paper.
2024: trains without tensor parallelism (pipeline 16, expert 64, ZeRO-1 data parallel), but serves with 4-way TP plus sequence parallelism for attention.

kb.t: Bounding the memory bottlenecks of large mixture-of-experts training
kb.n: 2026: the same memory accounting (weights, optimizer state, activations per GPU) applied to MoE training.

topics.n: tensor parallelism as the default way to serve a model across several GPUs.
NVLink and NVSwitch bandwidth as the constraint that keeps tensor parallelism inside one machine.
pipeline schedules (1F1B, DualPipe) and expert placement: the axes that took over from TP there.

verdict: Trust the mechanism fully: it is exact algebra, and every later training and serving stack uses it. Read the 76% as weak scaling in model size against a strong baseline, not as a speedup, and the state-of-the-art results as single runs on different training data.
